sentences.zh: 盧文進

translations.literal: Lu Wenjin
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenjin

sentences.zh: 盧文進，字大用，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Wenjin, courtesy name Dayong, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenjin, styled Dayong, came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 為劉守光騎將。

translations.literal: He was a cavalry commander for Liu Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Shouguang as a cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗攻范陽，文進以先降拜壽州刺史，莊宗以屬其弟存矩。

translations.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong attacked Fanyang, Wenjin surrendered early and was made prefect of Shouzhou; Zhuangzong placed him under his younger brother Cunju.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong attacked Fanyang, Wenjin surrendered first and was made prefect of Shou. Zhuangzong put him under his brother Cunju.

sentences.zh: 存矩為新州團練使，統山後八軍。

translations.literal: Cunju was training commissioner of Xin prefecture and commanded the eight armies north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Cunju was training commissioner of Xin and commanded the eight armies of the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與劉鄩相拒於莘，召存矩會兵擊鄩。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and Liu Xun faced each other at Xin; he summoned Cunju to unite forces and strike Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and Liu Xun were locked at Xin. He called Cunju to join forces and strike Xun.

sentences.zh: 存矩募山後勁兵數千人，課民出馬，民以十牛易一馬，山後之人皆怨，而兵又不樂南行，行至祁溝關，聚而謀為亂。

translations.literal: Cunju recruited several thousand elite troops from north of the mountains and levied horses from the people; the people traded ten oxen for one horse, and all north of the mountains resented it, while the soldiers also disliked marching south; when they reached Qigou Pass they gathered and plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Cunju raised several thousand crack troops from the northern hills and forced the people to furnish horses—ten oxen for one mount—and the hill folk seethed while the soldiers loathed the southward march. At Qigou Pass they gathered to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 文進有女幼而美，存矩求之為側室，文進以其大將不敢拒，雖與，心常歉之也，因與亂軍殺存矩反。

translations.literal: Wenjin had a daughter, young and beautiful; Cunju asked for her as a concubine. Wenjin, because Cunju was a great general, dared not refuse; though he gave her, his heart always bore a grudge, and he therefore joined the mutineers in killing Cunju and rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin had a young, beautiful daughter. Cunju demanded her as a side wife. Wenjin dared not refuse so great a commander, yet his heart never forgave it; he joined the mutineers, killed Cunju, and turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 攻新州，不克，攻武州，又不克，遂奔於契丹，契丹使守平州。

translations.literal: He attacked Xin prefecture but could not take it, attacked Wu prefecture and again could not take it, then fled to the Khitan, and the Khitan made him guard Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Xin and failed, struck Wu and failed again, then fled to the Khitan, who set him to hold Ping.

sentences.zh: 文進身長七尺，狀貌偉然。

translations.literal: Wenjin stood seven feet in height, his bearing imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin stood seven feet tall, his bearing imposing.

sentences.zh: 自其奔契丹也，數引契丹攻掠幽、薊之間，虜其人民，教契丹以中國織纴工作無不備，契丹由此益強。

translations.literal: From the time he fled to the Khitan he repeatedly led Khitan forces to raid between You and Ji, carried off the people, and taught the Khitan every Chinese craft of weaving and manufacture—nothing was lacking—and the Khitan thereby grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had fled to the Khitan he led them again and again against You and Ji, carried off people, and taught them Chinese weaving and every craft—nothing was wanting—and the Khitan grew the stronger for it.

sentences.zh: 同光中，契丹數以奚騎出入塞上，攻掠燕、趙，人無寧歲。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era the Khitan repeatedly sent Xi horsemen in and out beyond the passes, raiding Yan and Zhao, and the people knew no year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tongguang the Khitan sent Xi horse across the border year after year, harrying Yan and Zhao, and the people knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 唐兵屯涿州，歲時饋運，自瓦橋關至幽州，嚴兵斥候，常苦鈔奪，為唐患者十餘年，皆文進為之也。

translations.literal: Tang troops were stationed at Zhuozhou; each year supplies were transported from Waqiao Pass to Youzhou under strict scouts and patrols, yet they constantly suffered plunder—more than ten years of trouble for Tang, all wrought by Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang held Zhuo. Every year convoys ran from Waqiao Pass to Youzhou under heavy escort, yet they were robbed without cease—for more than ten years Tang’s affliction was Wenjin’s doing.

sentences.zh: 及其南奔，始屈身晦跡，務為恭謹，禮接文士，謙謙若不足，其所談論，近代朝廷儀制、臺閣故事而已，未嘗言兵。

translations.literal: When he fled south he at last bent his person and hid his tracks, striving for deference and caution, treating scholars with courtesy, humble as though insufficient; what he discussed was only recent court ritual and Secretariat precedent—he never spoke of war.
translations.idiomatic: When he fled south he bent low and hid his trail, all deference and caution, courteous to literati, humble as if he were nothing. He spoke only of recent court ritual and Secretariat lore—never of war.

sentences.zh: 後以左衛上將軍卒於金陵。

translations.literal: Later he died at Jinling as Senior General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at Jinling as Senior General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 李金全

translations.literal: Li Jinquan
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinquan

sentences.zh: 李金全，其先出於吐渾。

translations.literal: Li Jinquan—his ancestors came from the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinquan’s people came from the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 金全少為唐明宗廝養，以驍勇善騎射，常從明宗戰伐，以功為刺史。

translations.literal: In youth Jinquan was raised in Mingzong’s household service; for valor and skill in riding and archery he often followed Mingzong in campaigns and, by merit, became a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan was raised in Mingzong’s household as a boy. Bold in the saddle and with the bow, he rode on Mingzong’s campaigns and rose to prefect by merit.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為彰義軍節度使，在鎮務為貪暴。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was military commissioner of the Zhangyi army and in his circuit strove to be greedy and brutal.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng he held the Zhangyi circuit and ruled it with greed and violence.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，獻馬數十匹，居數日，又以獻，明宗謂曰：「卿患馬多邪，何進獻之數也？

translations.literal: Dismissed and returned, he presented several tens of horses; within days he presented again. Mingzong said to him: “Do you suffer from too many horses, that you present them so often?
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from office, he sent several dozen horses; within days he sent more. Mingzong said: “Do you have too many horses, that you keep offering them?

sentences.zh: 且卿在涇州治狀如何，無乃以馬為事乎？

translations.literal: And how was your governance in Jingzhou—were you perhaps busy with horses alone?
translations.idiomatic: And how did you govern Jing—were horses your only business?

sentences.zh: 」金全慚不能對。

translations.literal: ” Jinquan was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jinquan flushed and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮橫海。

translations.literal: He was transferred to hold the Transoceanic circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Transoceanic circuit.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷為右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was dismissed and made Senior General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was stripped of his post and made Senior General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，安州屯防指揮使王暉殺節度使周瑰，高祖遣金全將騎兵千人以往，下詔書招暉曰：「暉降，以為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: In Gaozu’s time, Wang Hui, garrison commander of Anzhou, killed Military Commissioner Zhou Gui; Gaozu sent Jinquan with a thousand horsemen, and issued an edict to summon Hui, saying: “If Hui surrenders, make him prefect of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Gaozu, Wang Hui of Anzhou’s garrison command killed Commissioner Zhou Gui. Gaozu sent Jinquan with a thousand horse and issued an edict: “If Hui yields, make him prefect of Tang.

sentences.zh: 」又以信箭諭安州，不戮一人，且戒金全曰：「無失吾信。

translations.literal: ” He also sent a credentialed arrow to proclaim Anzhou, that not one person be slain, and warned Jinquan: “Do not break my faith.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent a trust-arrow to Anzhou pledging not a single life, and charged Jinquan: “Do not break my word.

sentences.zh: 」金全未至，襄州安從進意暉必走江南，以精兵遮其要路。

translations.literal: ” Before Jinquan arrived, An Congjin of Xiangzhou judged that Hui would surely flee to the southland and sent elite troops to block the critical roads.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jinquan had not yet arrived when An Congjin of Xiang judged Hui would flee south and sent crack troops to cut the roads.

sentences.zh: 暉聞金全來，果南走，為從進兵所殺。

translations.literal: Hui heard Jinquan was coming, fled south as expected, and was killed by Congjin’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hui heard Jinquan was near, fled south as expected, and Congjin’s men killed him.

sentences.zh: 金全後至，得暉餘黨數百人，皆送京師。

translations.literal: Jinquan arrived later, took several hundred of Hui’s remnant partisans, and sent them all to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan came after, seized several hundred of Hui’s remnant band, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 暉之亂也，大掠城中三日，金全利其所掠貲，因擒其將武克和等十餘人殺之，克和呼曰：「王暉首亂，猶賜之信誓，以為刺史；

translations.literal: In Hui’s rebellion the city was greatly plundered for three days; Jinquan coveted the loot and therefore seized his generals Wu Kehe and more than ten others and killed them. Kehe cried out: “Wang Hui was first to rebel, yet he was still granted a sworn pledge and made prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Hui’s revolt had let the city be plundered three days. Jinquan coveted the spoil, seized generals such as Wu Kehe—more than ten—and killed them. Kehe shouted: “Wang Hui led the mutiny yet won a sworn pledge and a prefecture;

sentences.zh: 我等何罪，反見殺邪？

translations.literal: what crime have we, that we are killed instead?
translations.idiomatic: what crime is ours, that we alone are slain?

sentences.zh: 若朝廷之命，何以示信？

translations.literal: If this is the court’s command, how will faith be shown?
translations.idiomatic: If this is the throne’s order, how will anyone trust its word?

sentences.zh: 茍將軍違詔而殺降，亦將不免也！

translations.literal: If the general disobeys the edict and kills those who surrender, he too will not escape!
translations.idiomatic: If you defy the edict and kill men who yielded, you will not escape either!

sentences.zh: 」高祖不能詰。

translations.literal: ” Gaozu could not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gaozu could not call him to account.

sentences.zh: 即以金全為安遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: Jinquan was at once made military commissioner of the Anyuan army.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan was at once made commissioner of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 金全左都押衙明漢榮用事，所為不法，高祖患之，不欲因漢榮以累功臣，為選廉吏賈仁沼代之，且召漢榮。

translations.literal: Jinquan’s Left Commandant of the Headquarters Guard Ming Hanrong wielded power and acted unlawfully; Gaozu was troubled by it, yet did not wish to burden a meritorious minister because of Hanrong, and therefore chose the honest official Jia Renzhao to replace him and also summoned Hanrong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan’s Left Commandant Ming Hanrong held real power and broke the law. Gaozu resented it but would not ruin a meritorious man on Hanrong’s account; he chose the upright Jia Renzhao to replace him and summoned Hanrong as well.

sentences.zh: 漢榮教金全留己而不遣，金全客龐令圖諫曰：「仁沼昔事王晏球，晏球攻王都於中山，都遣善射者登城射晏球，中兜牟，仁沼從後引弓，射善射者，一發而斃，晏球求其人，欲厚賞之，仁沼退而不言，此天下之忠臣也。

translations.literal: Hanrong urged Jinquan to keep him and not send him away. Jinquan’s retainer Pang Lingtu remonstrated, saying: “Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu. When Yanqiu attacked Wang Du at Zhongshan, Du sent a fine archer to the wall to shoot Yanqiu and hit his helmet tassel; Renzhao drew from behind, shot the archer, and dropped him with one arrow. Yanqiu sought the man to reward him richly, but Renzhao withdrew and would not speak—this is a loyal man under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hanrong taught Jinquan to detain him and refuse the summons. Client Pang Lingtu urged: “Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu. When Yanqiu besieged Wang Du at Zhongshan, Du put a crack bowman on the wall who struck Yanqiu’s helmet tassel. Renzhao drew from behind, one arrow, and the bowman fell. Yanqiu hunted for the man to reward him; Renzhao stayed silent—that is loyalty under heaven.

sentences.zh: 都敗，晏球遣仁沼獻捷於京師，凡所賜與甚厚，悉以分故人、親戚之貧者，此天下之廉士也。

translations.literal: When Du was defeated Yanqiu sent Renzhao to present the victory at the capital; all he was given was very generous, yet he divided it entirely among old friends and poor kin—this is an honest man under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Du fell, Yanqiu sent Renzhao to report victory at court. Every gift was rich, yet he gave it all to old friends and poor kin—that is honesty under heaven.

sentences.zh: 為人如此，豈有為人謀而不善者乎？

translations.literal: A man like this—how could he scheme for others and not do well?
translations.idiomatic: Such a man—how could he serve you ill?

sentences.zh: 宜納仁沼而遣漢榮。

translations.literal: You should accept Renzhao and send Hanrong away.
translations.idiomatic: Take Renzhao in and send Hanrong off.

sentences.zh: 」漢榮聞之，夜使人殺令圖而冘仁沼，仁沼舌壞而死。

translations.literal: ” Hanrong heard of it, and by night sent men to kill Lingtu and poison Renzhao; Renzhao’s tongue rotted and he died.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hanrong heard, and that night had Lingtu killed and Renzhao poisoned; Renzhao’s tongue putrefied and he died.

sentences.zh: 天福五年夏，高祖以馬全節代金全。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, summer, Gaozu replaced Jinquan with Ma Quanjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianfu, summer, Gaozu sent Ma Quanjie to replace Jinquan.

sentences.zh: 而仁沼二子欲詣京師訴其父冤，漢榮大懼，紿金全曰：「前日天子召漢榮，公違詔而不遣。

translations.literal: Renzhao’s two sons wished to go to the capital to plead their father’s wrong; Hanrong was greatly afraid and deceived Jinquan, saying: “The other day the Son of Heaven summoned Hanrong, yet you disobeyed the edict and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhao’s two sons meant to go to court to plead their father’s wrong. Hanrong was terrified and lied to Jinquan: “The throne summoned Hanrong the other day, yet you defied the edict and kept him.

sentences.zh: 仁沼之死，其二子將訴於朝。

translations.literal: With Renzhao’s death, his two sons will sue at court.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhao is dead; his sons will sue at court.

sentences.zh: 今以全節代公，是召公對獄也。

translations.literal: Now Quanjie replaces you—that is to summon you to answer at trial.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie is sent in your place—that is to call you before the law.

sentences.zh: 」金全信之，遂叛，送款於李。

translations.literal: ” Jinquan believed it, then rebelled and sent allegiance to Li.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jinquan believed him, rebelled, and submitted to Li Bian.

sentences.zh: 高祖發兵三萬授全節討之。

translations.literal: Gaozu raised thirty thousand troops and gave them to Quanjie to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu raised thirty thousand men and gave Quanjie command to crush him.

sentences.zh: 遣其將李承裕入安州，金全遂南奔，行至泌川，引頸北望，涕泣而去。

translations.literal: He sent his general Li Chengyu into Anzhou; Jinquan then fled south. When he reached Mishui he stretched his neck to look north, wept, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Chengyu into An. Jinquan fled south. At Mishui he craned his neck northward, wept, and went on.

sentences.zh: 以金全為天威統軍。

translations.literal: Li made Jinquan commander of the Heavenly Might army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian made him commander of the Heavenly Might army.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝時，李守貞反河中，乞兵於，金全為潤州節度使，與查文徽等出沐陽。

translations.literal: Under Han’s Emperor Yin, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and begged troops of —; Jinquan was military commissioner of Runzhou and, with Zha Wenhui and others, marched out of Shuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han’s Emperor Yin, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and begged troops of Li Bian. Jinquan, as Li Bian’s Runzhou commissioner, marched with Zha Wenhui and others out of Shuyang.

sentences.zh: 之諸將皆銳於攻取，金全獨以謂遠不相及，不可行，乃止。

translations.literal: —’s generals were all keen to attack; Jinquan alone judged that the distance made it impossible and would not go, and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian’s generals were eager to strike; Jinquan alone said the distance made it futile, and they halted.

sentences.zh: 其後亦不復用，不知其所終。

translations.literal: Afterward he was never again employed; no one knows how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: He was never employed again; his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 楊思權

translations.literal: Yang Siquan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Siquan

sentences.zh: 楊思權，邠州新平人也。

translations.literal: Yang Siquan was a native of Xinping in Bin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Siquan came from Xinping in Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 事梁為控鶴右第一軍使。

translations.literal: He served Liang as commander of the first right Crane-Control army.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as first commander of the right Crane-Control corps.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，以為夾馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, he was made commander of the Flanking Horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, he was made Flanking Horse commander.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，秦王從榮為河東節度使，以馮赟為副，思權為北京步軍都指揮使以佐佑之。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong the Prince of Qin, Congrong, was military commissioner of Hedong; Feng Yun was made his deputy, and Siquan was metropolitan infantry commander of the Northern Capital to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong, Prince of Qin Congrong held Hedong; Feng Yun was his deputy and Siquan metropolitan infantry commander of the Northern Capital to support him.

sentences.zh: 從榮素驕，所為多不法。

translations.literal: Congrong was by nature arrogant and his acts were mostly unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was proud by nature and his deeds were mostly lawless.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋王從厚為河南尹。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Song, Conghou, was metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince of Song Conghou was metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 從厚年少，謙恭好禮。

translations.literal: Conghou was young, modest, and fond of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Conghou was young, courteous, and fond of propriety.

sentences.zh: 明宗陰遣人從容語從厚之善，以諷勉之。

translations.literal: Mingzong secretly sent men to speak at ease of Conghou’s virtues, to admonish and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong secretly had men speak gently of Conghou’s virtues to admonish and encourage Congrong.

sentences.zh: 從榮不悅，告思權曰：「天下共賢河南而非我，我將廢矣，奈何？

translations.literal: Congrong was displeased and told Siquan: “All under heaven praise Henan and not me—I am about to be deposed; what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was displeased and told Siquan: “The realm praises Henan, not me—I shall be cast aside. What then?

sentences.zh: 」思權曰：「公有甲士，而思權在，何患也！

translations.literal: ” Siquan said: “Your Highness has armored men, and while Siquan is here, what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: ” Siquan said: “Your Highness has mailed men, and with Siquan at hand, why fear?

sentences.zh: 」乃勸從榮招募死士、增利器械以為備。

translations.literal: ” He therefore urged Congrong to recruit dare-to-die soldiers and improve weapons as preparation.
translations.idiomatic: ” He urged Congrong to recruit dare-to-die men and sharpen arms against the day.

sentences.zh: 馮赟患之，以其事聞。

translations.literal: Feng Yun was troubled by it and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun was alarmed and reported it.

sentences.zh: 明宗召思權還京師，以從榮故，亦不之責也。

translations.literal: Mingzong summoned Siquan back to the capital; because of Congrong he did not punish him either.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong recalled Siquan to the capital; for Congrong’s sake he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 後為右羽林都指揮使，將兵戍興元。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Feathered-Lin commander and led troops to garrison Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Right Feathered-Lin commander and garrisoned Xingyuan with troops.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反鳳翔，興元張虔釗會諸鎮兵討賊。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, Congke, rebelled at Fengxiang; Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan united the circuit armies to suppress the traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang. Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan united the circuit armies against him.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮兵圍鳳翔，思權攻城西，嚴衛指揮使尹暉攻城東，破其兩關城。

translations.literal: The circuit armies besieged Fengxiang; Siquan assaulted the west wall and Yin Hui, commander of the Stern Guard, assaulted the east wall, breaching both outer gate-cities.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits besieged Fengxiang. Siquan stormed the west; Yin Hui of the Stern Guard stormed the east—they broke both outer gate-cities.

sentences.zh: 從珂登城呼外兵，告以己非反者，其語甚哀，外兵聞者皆悲之，而虔釗督戰甚急，軍士反兵逐虔釗，思權因呼其眾曰：「潞王真吾主也！

translations.literal: Congke climbed the wall and called to the troops outside, telling them he was no rebel; his words were very mournful, and those outside who heard were all grieved, yet Qianzhao pressed the battle fiercely; the soldiers turned their weapons and drove Qianzhao off, and Siquan therefore shouted to his masses: “The Prince of Lu is truly our lord!
translations.idiomatic: Congke mounted the wall and called to the army outside that he was no rebel; his words were pitiful, and hearers wept. Yet Qianzhao drove the fight hard. The men turned on Qianzhao and drove him off. Siquan shouted: “Prince of Lu is our true lord!

sentences.zh: 」即擁軍士入城降。

translations.literal: ” He at once led the soldiers into the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: ” and led his men into the city in surrender.

sentences.zh: 暉聞思權已降，亦麾其軍使解甲，由是諸鎮之兵皆潰。

translations.literal: When Hui heard Siquan had surrendered, he too waved his army to doff armor, and thereby the armies of all the circuits collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui heard Siquan had yielded and ordered his own men to unarm; the circuit hosts melted away.

sentences.zh: 思權與暉入見從珂，思權前曰：「臣以赤心奉殿下，殿下事成，願不以防禦、團練使處臣。

translations.literal: Siquan and Hui entered to see Congke; Siquan stepped forward and said: “Your servant offers a loyal heart to Your Highness; when Your Highness succeeds, I beg you not to place me as defense or training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Siquan and Hui came before Congke. Siquan said: “I serve Your Highness with a loyal heart; when you succeed, do not make me a defense or training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 」乃出一紙於懷中曰：「願誌臣姓名以為驗。

translations.literal: ” He then produced a paper from his bosom and said: “I beg you record my name as proof.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drew a paper from his robe: “Record my name as proof.

sentences.zh: 」從珂即書曰：「可邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: ” Congke at once wrote: “May have the Binning military commission.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congke wrote at once: “Granted Binning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 」廢帝入立，拜思權靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: ” When the deposed emperor entered and took the throne, Siquan was made military commissioner of the Jingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: ” When the deposed emperor took the throne, Siquan was made Jingnan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 後為右龍武統軍、左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Dragon Martial commander and Senior General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Right Dragon Martial commander and Senior General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 天福八年，卒於京師，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died at the capital and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died at the capital; the court posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 尹暉者，魏州大名人也。

translations.literal: Yin Hui was a native of Daming in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hui came from Daming in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 從廢帝入洛陽，而晉高祖來朝，與暉遇於道。

translations.literal: He followed the deposed emperor into Luoyang; Jin Gaozu came to court and met Hui on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the deposed emperor into Luoyang. Jin Gaozu came to court and met Hui on the road.

sentences.zh: 暉時猶為嚴衛指揮使，恃先降功，不為高祖屈，馬上橫鞭揖之，高祖怒，白廢帝暉不可與名藩。

translations.literal: Hui was still Stern Guard commander; relying on his merit in surrendering first, he would not bow to Gaozu and, on horseback, saluted with his whip across his body. Gaozu was angry and told the deposed emperor that Hui should not be given a famous circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was still Stern Guard commander. Trusting in his early surrender, he would not yield to Gaozu and saluted from the saddle with whip athwart. Gaozu was furious and told the deposed emperor Hui must not receive a great circuit.

sentences.zh: 乃以為應州節度使。

translations.literal: He was therefore made military commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made commissioner of Ying.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，罷為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, Hui was dismissed and made Grand General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, Hui was reduced to Grand General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 範延光反，以書招暉，暉懼，出奔淮南，為人所殺，有子勛。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang rebelled and sent a letter to recruit Hui; Hui was afraid, fled south to Huainan, and was killed by another; he had a son Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang rebelled and wrote to win Hui. Hui was afraid, fled to Huainan, and was killed; he left a son Xun.

sentences.zh: 王弘贄

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhi

sentences.zh: 王弘贄，不知其世家何人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhi—no one knows what his family lineage was.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhi—his lineage is unknown.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗時，為合階二州刺史、右千牛衛將軍、衛州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Tang’s Mingzong he was prefect of He and Jie, general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was prefect of He and Jie, general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反於鳳翔，擁兵東至陜。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu, Congke, rebelled at Fengxiang he led troops east as far as Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang he marched east with troops as far as Shan.

sentences.zh: 湣帝懼，夜以百餘騎出奔，至衛州東七八里，遇晉高祖將朝於京師，騶呵前導者不避，湣帝遣左右叱之，對曰：「成德軍節度使石敬瑭也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Min was afraid; at night he fled with a little more than a hundred horsemen. Seven or eight li east of Weizhou he met Jin Gaozu, who was about to attend court at the capital; the outriders who cleared the way before him would not yield, and the emperor sent attendants to shout them down; they answered: “It is Shi Jingtang, military commissioner of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min was terrified. At night he fled with a little over a hundred horse. Seven or eight li east of Wei he met Jin Gaozu bound for court. The outriders clearing the road would not give way; the emperor sent men to shout them down. They answered: “Shi Jingtang, commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 」湣帝即下馬慟哭，謂敬瑭曰：「潞王反，康義誠等皆叛我，我無所依，長公主教我逆爾於路。

translations.literal: ” The emperor at once dismounted and wept, saying to Jingtang: “The Prince of Lu has rebelled; Kang Yicheng and the rest have all betrayed me; I have nowhere to rely; the Grand Princess told me to meet you on the road.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor dismounted at once and wept. He told Jingtang: “Prince of Lu has rebelled. Kang Yicheng and the rest have betrayed me. I have nowhere to turn. The Grand Princess bade me meet you on the road.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「衛州刺史王弘贄，宿將也，且多知時事，請就圖之。

translations.literal: ” Gaozu said: “Wei Prefect Wang Hongzhi is an old commander and knows the times well—let us go consult him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gaozu said: “Wang Hongzhi of Wei is an old soldier and knows the times—let us consult him.

sentences.zh: 」即馳騎前見弘贄曰：「主上危迫，吾戚屬也，何以圖全？

translations.literal: ” He at once galloped ahead to see Hongzhi and said: “The sovereign is in peril; I am his kin—how may we secure safety?
translations.idiomatic: ” He galloped ahead to Hongzhi: “The Son of Heaven is in peril. I am kin—how do we keep him whole?

sentences.zh: 」弘贄曰：「天子避狄，自古有之，然將相大臣從乎？

translations.literal: ” Hongzhi said: “Emperors fleeing barbarians—there has been such since antiquity; yet do chief ministers and great officials follow?
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongzhi said: “Sons of Heaven flee barbarians—so it has been since antiquity. But do ministers and great officials follow?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「無也。

translations.literal: ” He said: “None.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said: “None.

sentences.zh: 」「國寶、乘輿、法物從乎？

translations.literal: ”“Do the state treasures, the imperial carriage, and ritual objects follow?
translations.idiomatic: ”“Do the state treasures, the imperial carriage, and the ritual regalia follow?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「無也。

translations.literal: ” He said: “None.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said: “None.

sentences.zh: 」弘贄嘆曰：「所謂大木將顛，非一繩所維。

translations.literal: ” Hongzhi sighed and said: “What they call ‘the great tree is about to fall—one rope cannot hold it.’
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongzhi sighed: “As they say, the great tree is about to fall—one rope cannot hold it.

sentences.zh: 今萬乘之主，以百騎出奔，而將相大臣無一人從者，則人心去就可知也。

translations.literal: Now the lord of ten thousand chariots flees with a hundred horsemen, and not one minister or great official follows—then where the people’s hearts have gone may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Son of Heaven flees with a hundred horse, and not one minister follows—you can read where hearts have gone.

sentences.zh: 雖欲興復，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Even if you wished to restore the realm, how could it be attained!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you wished to restore him, how could you?

sentences.zh: 」即從高祖上謁於驛舍。

translations.literal: ” He then followed Gaozu to present himself at the post station.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then followed Gaozu to attend the emperor at the relay house.

sentences.zh: 高祖且以弘贄語白湣帝。

translations.literal: Gaozu then reported Hongzhi’s words to the Lamented Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then told the Lamented Emperor what Hongzhi had said.

sentences.zh: 弓箭庫使沙守榮、奔弘進前謂高祖曰：「主上，明宗愛子，公，愛婿也，公於此時不能報國，而反問大臣、國寶所在，公亦助賊反邪？

translations.literal: Bow-and-arrow depot commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin advanced and said to Gaozu: “Your Lordship is Emperor Mingzong’s beloved son, and you his beloved son-in-law—at such a time you cannot repay the state but instead ask where the ministers and state treasures are; do you too aid the rebels?”
translations.idiomatic: Bow-and-arrow depot commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin came forward and said to Gaozu: “Your Lordship is Mingzong’s beloved son and his beloved son-in-law. At such a time you cannot repay the state yet ask where the ministers and the state treasures are—do you aid the rebels?”

sentences.zh: 」乃抽佩刀刺高祖，高祖親將陳暉捍之，守榮與暉戰死，弘進亦自刎。

translations.literal: ” They then drew their girdle daggers to stab Gaozu; Gaozu’s personal guard Chen Hui parried them; Shourong and Hui died fighting, and Hongjin cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: ” They drew their girdle daggers to stab Gaozu. His personal guard Chen Hui parried; Shourong and Hui died fighting, and Hongjin cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 高祖因盡殺帝從兵，獨留帝於驛而去。

translations.literal: Gaozu then killed all the emperor’s attendant troops, left the emperor alone at the post station, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then killed all the emperor’s escort troops, left the emperor alone at the post station, and went away.

sentences.zh: 弘贄奉帝居於州廨。

translations.literal: Hongzhi housed the emperor in the prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi lodged the emperor in the prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 弘贄有子巒，為殿直，廢帝入立，遣巒持鴆與弘贄。

translations.literal: Hongzhi had a son Luan, a palace attendants director; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne he sent Luan with poisoned wine to Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi had a son Luan, a palace attendants director. When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he sent Luan with poisoned wine for Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，湣帝在衛州，弘贄令市中酒家獻酒，湣帝見之，大驚，遽殞於地，久而蘇，弘贄曰：「此酒家也，願獻酒以慰無憀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Lamented Emperor was at Weizhou, Hongzhi had a city wine-shop keeper present wine; the emperor was greatly startled, fell at once, long lay unconscious, then revived; Hongzhi said: “This is a wine-shop keeper—he wished to present wine to comfort your boredom.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Weizhou, Hongzhi had a city wine-shop keeper present wine. The emperor was greatly startled, fell at once, long lay senseless, then revived. Hongzhi said: “This is a wine-shop keeper—he wished to offer wine and ease your boredom.

sentences.zh: 」湣帝受之，由是日獻一觴。

translations.literal: ” The Lamented Emperor accepted it; thereafter one cup was presented daily.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Lamented Emperor accepted it; thereafter one cup came each day.

sentences.zh: 及巒持鴆至，因使酒家獻之，湣帝飲而不疑，遂崩。

translations.literal: When Luan brought the poisoned wine, he again had the wine-shop present it; the Lamented Emperor drank without suspicion and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan brought the poisoned wine, the wine-shop presented it again. The Lamented Emperor drank without suspicion and died.

sentences.zh: 弘贄後事晉為鳳翔行軍司馬，以光祿卿致仕，卒，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Hongzhi later served Jin as Fengxiang campaign marshal, retired as Minister of the Imperial Clan, died, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi later served Jin as Fengxiang campaign marshal, retired as Minister of the Imperial Clan, died, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 劉審交

translations.literal: Liu Shenjiao
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenjiao

sentences.zh: 劉審交，字求益，幽州文安人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shenjiao, style name Qiuyi, was a man of Wen’an in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenjiao, styled Qiuyi, came from Wen’an in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少略知書，通於吏事，為唐興令，補范陽牙校。

translations.literal: In youth he knew books somewhat and was skilled at clerkly affairs; he was Tang’s Xing prefect and made up as a Fanyang yamen officer.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he knew books somewhat and was skilled at clerkly work. He was Tang’s Xing prefect and made up as a Fanyang yamen officer.

sentences.zh: 劉守光僭號，以審交為兵部尚書，守光敗，歸於太原，唐莊宗以為從事。

translations.literal: When Liu Shouguang declared himself emperor, he made Shenjiao Minister of War; when Shouguang fell he returned to Taiyuan and Zhuangzong made him a staff associate.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang declared himself emperor, he made Shenjiao Minister of War. Shouguang fell; he returned to Taiyuan and Zhuangzong made him a staff associate.

sentences.zh: 其後趙德鈞鎮范陽，北面轉運使馬紹宏辟審交判官。

translations.literal: Later Zhao Dejun held Fanyang; northern transport commissioner Ma Shaohong recruited Shenjiao as registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao Dejun held Fanyang. Northern transport commissioner Ma Shaohong took Shenjiao as registrar.

sentences.zh: 王晏球討王都，以為轉運供軍使。

translations.literal: Wang Yanqiu campaigned against Wang Du; he was made transport commissioner supplying the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanqiu campaigned against Wang Du; Shenjiao was made transport commissioner supplying the army.

sentences.zh: 定州平，拜遼州刺史。

translations.literal: When Dingzhou was pacified he was made Liaozhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingzhou was pacified he was made Liaozhou governor.

sentences.zh: 復為北面轉運使，改慈州刺史，以母老去官。

translations.literal: Again northern transport commissioner, then Cizhou governor; he left office because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Again northern transport commissioner, then Cizhou governor; he left office because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哀毀過禮，不調累年。

translations.literal: On his mother’s death his grief exceeded ritual; he took no post for many years.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother’s death his grief exceeded ritual; he held no post for many years.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖即位，楊光遠討範延光於魏州，審交復為供軍使。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne Yang Guangyuan campaigned against Fan Yanguang at Weizhou; Shenjiao was again supply commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s Gaozu took the throne Yang Guangyuan campaigned against Fan Yanguang at Weizhou. Shenjiao was again supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉高祖分戶部、度支、鹽鐵為三使，歲餘，三司益煩弊，乃復合為一，拜審交三司使。

translations.literal: At that time Jin Gaozu split Household, Revenue, and Salt-Iron into three bureaus; after a year the three bureaus grew more tangled; they were merged into one again and Shenjiao was made Three-Bureaus commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s Gaozu had split Household, Revenue, and Salt-Iron into three bureaus. After a year the three grew more tangled; they were merged again and Shenjiao was made Three-Bureaus commissioner.

sentences.zh: 議者請檢天下民田，宜得益租，審交曰：「租有定額，而天下比年無閑田，民之苦樂，不可等也。

translations.literal: Counsellors proposed inspecting all the realm’s farmland to increase rent yields. Shenjiao said: “Rent has a fixed quota, yet in recent years the realm has had no idle fields; the people’s hardship and ease cannot be equated.
translations.idiomatic: Counsellors proposed inspecting all the realm’s farmland to raise rent. Shenjiao said: “Rent has a fixed quota, yet in recent years the realm has had no idle fields—the people’s hardship and ease cannot be equated.

sentences.zh: 」遂止不檢，而民賴以不擾。

translations.literal: ” Inspection was therefore halted, and the people were spared disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: ” Inspection was halted, and the people were spared disturbance.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛上將軍、陳州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was moved to senior general of the Right Guards and Chenzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to senior general of the Right Guards and Chenzhou defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 出視民田，見民耕器薄陋，乃取河北耕器為範，為民更鑄。

translations.literal: Going out to inspect the people’s fields he saw their farm tools were thin and crude; he took Hebei farm tools as models and had them recast for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the people’s fields he saw their farm tools were thin and crude. He took Hebei tools as models and had them recast for the people.

sentences.zh: 安從進平，徙審交襄州，又徙青州，皆有善政。

translations.literal: After An Congjin was pacified Shenjiao was moved to Xiangzhou, then Qingzhou—both with good government.
translations.idiomatic: After An Congjin was pacified Shenjiao was moved to Xiangzhou, then Qingzhou—both with good government.

sentences.zh: 罷還。

translations.literal: He was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯京師，留蕭翰而去，翰復以審交為三司使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital and left Xiao Han behind, Han again made Shenjiao Three-Bureaus commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan invaded the capital and left Xiao Han behind. Han again made Shenjiao Three-Bureaus commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而翰召許王從益守京師。

translations.literal: Before long Han summoned the Prince of Xu Congyi to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Han summoned the Prince of Xu Congyi to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖起義太原，從益召高行周以拒高祖，行周不至。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu raised a righteous army at Taiyuan; Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou to resist Han; Xingzhou did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu raised a righteous army at Taiyuan. Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou to resist Han; Xingzhou did not come.

sentences.zh: 從益母王淑妃與群臣謀迎高祖，或以謂燕兵在京師者猶數千，可以城守而待行周，淑妃不從，議未決。

translations.literal: Congyi’s mother the Princess Dowager Wang with ministers and officials deliberated welcoming Han Gaozu; some said Yan troops still in the capital numbered several thousand and they could hold the city and await Xingzhou; the princess dowager did not agree; the deliberation was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi’s mother the Princess Dowager Wang with ministers and officials deliberated welcoming Han Gaozu. Some said Yan troops in the capital still numbered several thousand and they could hold the city and await Xingzhou; the princess dowager did not agree; the deliberation was unresolved.

sentences.zh: 審交進曰：「余燕人也，今為燕守城，當為燕謀，然事勢不可為也。

translations.literal: Shenjiao advanced and said: “I am a Yan man; now I guard the city for Yan and should plan for Yan—yet the situation cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjiao advanced and said: “I am a Yan man. Now I guard the city for Yan and should plan for Yan—yet the situation cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 太妃語是。

translations.literal: The princess dowager said he was right.
translations.idiomatic: The princess dowager said he was right.

sentences.zh: 」從益乃罷不設備，遣人西迎高祖。

translations.literal: ” Congyi then ceased preparations, sent men west to welcome Han Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congyi then ceased preparations and sent men west to welcome Han Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖至，罷審交不用。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu arrived he dismissed Shenjiao from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu arrived he dismissed Shenjiao from office.

sentences.zh: 隱帝時，為汝州防禦使，有能名。

translations.literal: Under the Hidden Emperor he was Ruzhou defense commissioner and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hidden Emperor he was Ruzhou defense commissioner and had a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In Qianyou 3 he died aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyou 3 he died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 州人聚哭柩前，上疏乞留葬近郊，使民得歲時祠祭。

translations.literal: The prefecture’s people gathered weeping before his coffin and petitioned to bury him near the suburb so the people could offer seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture’s people gathered weeping before his coffin and petitioned to bury him near the suburb so they could offer seasonal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔特贈太尉，起祠立碑。

translations.literal: An edict specially posthumously made him Grand Marshal and raised a shrine and stele.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially posthumously made him Grand Marshal and raised a shrine and stele.

sentences.zh: 王周，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou, from Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少以勇力從軍，事唐莊宗、明宗，為裨校，以力戰有功拜刺史。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the army for courage, served Zhuangzong and Mingzong as a junior officer, and for fierce fighting was made a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he followed the army for courage, served Zhuangzong and Mingzong as a junior officer, and for fierce fighting was made a prefect.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，從楊光遠討範延光於魏州，又從杜重威討安重榮於鎮州，皆有功。

translations.literal: In Jin Tianfu he followed Yang Guangyuan against Fan Yanguang at Weizhou and Du Chongwei against An Chongrong at Zhenzhou—both with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu he followed Yang Guangyuan against Fan Yanguang at Weizhou and Du Chongwei against An Chongrong at Zhenzhou—both with merit.

sentences.zh: 歷貝州、涇州節度使。

translations.literal: He held Bei and Jing in succession as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He held Bei and Jing in succession as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 涇州張彥澤為政苛虐，民多流亡，周乃更為寬恕，問民疾苦，去其苛弊二十餘事，民皆復歸。

translations.literal: At Jing, Zhang Yanze’s government was harsh and cruel; many people fled. Zhou then made policy lenient, inquired into people’s hardships, and removed more than twenty harsh abuses; the people all returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Jing, Zhang Yanze’s rule was harsh and cruel and many fled. Zhou made policy lenient, inquired into people’s hardships, and removed more than twenty harsh abuses; the people all returned.

sentences.zh: 歷遷武勝、保義、義武、成德四鎮，皆有善政。

translations.literal: He was moved in succession through Wusheng, Baoyi, Yiwu, and Chengde—everywhere with good government.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved in succession through Wusheng, Baoyi, Yiwu, and Chengde—everywhere with good government.

sentences.zh: 定州橋壞，覆民租車，周曰：「橋梁不修，刺史過也。

translations.literal: At Dingzhou a bridge broke and overturned rent-grain carts. Zhou said: “Bridges not repaired are the prefect’s fault.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou a bridge broke and overturned rent-grain carts. Zhou said: “Bridges not repaired are the prefect’s fault.

sentences.zh: 」乃償民粟，為治其橋。

translations.literal: ” He compensated the people’s grain and repaired the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: ” He compensated the people’s grain and repaired the bridge.

sentences.zh: 杜重威降契丹，契丹兵過鎮州，臨城呼周使出降，周泣曰：「受晉厚恩，不能死戰而以城降，何面目面行見人主與士大夫乎！

translations.literal: Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan; Khitan troops passed Zhenzhou, called at the city for Zhou to come out and surrender. Zhou wept: “I received Jin’s deep grace—unable to fight to the death I surrender the city; what face dare I show the ruler and the gentlemen while still walking!
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan. Khitan troops passed Zhenzhou and called for Zhou to come out and surrender. Zhou wept: “Jin showed me deep grace—I could not fight to the death yet surrender the city. What face dare I show the ruler and the gentlemen while still walking!

sentences.zh: 」乃劇飲，求刀欲自引決，家人止之，迫以出降。

translations.literal: ” He then drank heavily, sought a knife to end himself; family stopped him; they forced him out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drank heavily and sought a knife to end himself. Family stopped him and forced him out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 契丹以周為武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Khitan made Zhou Wusheng military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan made Zhou Wusheng military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入立，徙鎮武寧。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne he was moved to Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu took the throne he was moved to Wuning.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮，贈中書令。

translations.literal: He died in his post and was posthumously made Palace Secretariat Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his post and was posthumously made Palace Secretariat Minister.

sentences.zh: 高行周

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou

sentences.zh: （行珪附）〉

translations.literal: (Xing Gui appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Xing Gui appended)〉

sentences.zh: 高行周，字尚質，媯州人也。

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou, style name Shangzhi, from Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, styled Shangzhi, came from Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 世為懷戎戍將。

translations.literal: For generations his family were garrison generals at Huairou.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family were garrison generals at Huairou.

sentences.zh: 父思繼。

translations.literal: Father Siji.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Siji.

sentences.zh: 思繼兄弟皆以武勇雄於北邊，為幽州節度使李匡威戍將。

translations.literal: Siji and his brothers were all martially fierce on the northern frontier, garrison generals for Youzhou military commissioner Li Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: Siji and his brothers were all martially fierce on the northern frontier—garrison generals for Youzhou military commissioner Li Kuangwei.

sentences.zh: 匡威為其弟匡儔所篡，晉王將討其亂，謀曰：「高思繼兄弟在孔領關，有兵三千，此後患也，不如遣人招之。

translations.literal: Kuangwei was usurped by his younger brother Kuangchou; the Prince of Jin would campaign to punish the disorder. The plan said: “Gao Siji and his brothers are at Kongling Pass with three thousand troops—they are a later trouble; better send men to recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei was usurped by his younger brother Kuangchou. The Prince of Jin would campaign to punish the disorder. The plan said: “Gao Siji and his brothers hold Kongling Pass with three thousand troops—a later trouble. Better send men to recruit them.

sentences.zh: 思繼為吾用，則事無不成。

translations.literal: If Siji serves us, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: If Siji serves us, nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 」克用遣人招思繼兄弟。

translations.literal: ” Li Keyong sent men to recruit the Siji brothers.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Prince of Jin sent men to recruit the Siji brothers.

sentences.zh: 燕俗重氣義，思繼等聞晉兵為匡威報仇，乃欣然從之，為晉兵前鋒。

translations.literal: Yan custom prized righteousness; hearing Jin troops were avenging Kuangwei, they gladly followed and were Jin’s vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan custom prized righteousness. Hearing Jin troops were avenging Kuangwei, they gladly followed and were Jin’s vanguard.

sentences.zh: 匡儔聞思繼兄弟皆叛，乃棄城走。

translations.literal: Hearing the Siji brothers had all defected, Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Siji brothers had all defected, Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 克用以劉仁恭守幽州，以其兄某為先鋒都指揮使，思繼為中軍都指揮使，弟某為後軍都指揮使，高氏兄弟分掌燕兵。

translations.literal: Li Keyong stationed Liu Rengong at Youzhou, made his elder brother Mo vanguard commander-in-chief, Siji central army commander-in-chief, and a younger brother Mo rear army commander-in-chief—the Gao brothers divided Yan troops among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin stationed Liu Rengong at Youzhou, made his elder brother vanguard commander-in-chief, Siji central army commander-in-chief, and a younger brother rear army commander-in-chief—the Gao brothers divided Yan troops among themselves.

sentences.zh: 克用臨決謂仁恭曰：「思繼兄弟，勢傾一方，為燕患者，必高氏也，宜善為防。

translations.literal: Li Keyong on parting told Rengong: “The Siji brothers’ power tilts one region—they are sure to be Yan’s affliction; you must guard well against them.
translations.idiomatic: On parting the Prince of Jin told Rengong: “The Siji brothers’ power tilts one region—they are sure to afflict Yan. Guard well against them.

sentences.zh: 」克用留晉兵千人為仁恭衛。

translations.literal: ” Li Keyong left a thousand Jin troops as Rengong’s guard.
translations.idiomatic: ” He left a thousand Jin troops as Rengong’s guard.

sentences.zh: 而晉兵多犯法，思繼等數誅殺之。

translations.literal: But the Jin troops often broke the law; Siji and the others repeatedly executed them.
translations.idiomatic: But the Jin troops often broke the law; Siji and the others repeatedly executed them.

sentences.zh: 克用以責仁恭，仁恭以高氏為訴，由是晉盡誅思繼兄弟。

translations.literal: Li Keyong blamed Rengong; Rengong pleaded the Gaos’ case—thereupon Jin executed the Siji brothers entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin blamed Rengong; Rengong pleaded the Gaos’ case—thereupon Jin executed the Siji brothers entirely.

sentences.zh: 仁恭以其兄某之子行珪為牙將，而思繼子行周年十餘歲，亦收之帳下，稍長，補以軍職。

translations.literal: Rengong made his elder brother Mo’s son Xinggui a yamen officer, and Xingzhou was barely over ten; he also took him into his tent; as he grew he was given military posts.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong made his elder brother’s son Xinggui a yamen officer. Xingzhou was barely over ten; he also took him into his tent; as he grew he was given military posts.

sentences.zh: 仁恭被囚，守光立，以行珪為武州刺史。

translations.literal: Rengong was imprisoned; Shouguang rose; he made Xinggui Wuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was imprisoned; Shouguang rose and made Xinggui Wuzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 其後守光背晉，晉兵攻之。

translations.literal: Later Shouguang turned against Jin; Jin troops attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shouguang turned against Jin; Jin troops attacked.

sentences.zh: 守光將元行欽牧馬山後，聞守光且見圍，即率所牧馬赴援，而麾下兵叛於道，推行欽為幽州留後，行欽曰：「吾所憚者行珪也。

translations.literal: Shouguang was about to have Yuan Xingqin herd horses beyond the mountains; hearing Shouguang was nearly besieged he at once led the herd to rescue; but his troops mutinied on the road, installed Xingqin as Youzhou regent. Xingqin said: “What I fear is Xinggui alone.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang was about to have Yuan Xingqin herd horses beyond the mountains. Hearing Shouguang was nearly besieged, he at once led the herd to rescue; but his troops mutinied on the road and installed Xingqin as Youzhou regent. Xingqin said: “What I fear is Xinggui alone.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣人之懷戎，得行珪子系之。

translations.literal: ” He sent men to Huairou and seized Xinggui’s son.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent men to Huairou and seized Xinggui’s son.

sentences.zh: 兵過武州，招行珪曰：「守光可取而代也。

translations.literal: The army passed Wuzhou and summoned Xinggui: “Shouguang can be taken and replaced.
translations.idiomatic: The army passed Wuzhou and summoned Xinggui: “Shouguang can be taken and replaced.

sentences.zh: 當從我行，不然，且殺公子。

translations.literal: Follow me or I kill your son.
translations.idiomatic: Follow me or I kill your son.

sentences.zh: 」行珪謝曰：「與君俱劉公將，而忍叛之？

translations.literal: ” Xinggui declined: “We were both General Liu’s officers—how bear to betray him?
translations.idiomatic: ” Xinggui declined: “We were both General Liu’s officers—how bear to betray him?

sentences.zh: 吾當為劉氏也，尚何顧吾子耶！

translations.literal: I must stand for the Liu house—what care I for my son!
translations.idiomatic: I must stand for the Liu house—what care I for my son!

sentences.zh: 」行欽即以兵圍行珪。

translations.literal: ” Xingqin then surrounded Xinggui with troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xingqin then surrounded Xinggui with troops.

sentences.zh: 月餘，行珪城中食盡，召其州人告曰：「吾非不為父老守也，今劉公救兵不至，奈何？

translations.literal: After more than a month the city’s food was exhausted; he summoned the prefecture people and said: “It is not that I will not guard you, elders—but Liu’s rescue troops have not come; what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the city’s food was exhausted. He summoned the prefecture people and said: “It is not that I will not guard you, elders—but Liu’s rescue troops have not come. What can be done?

sentences.zh: 可殺吾以降晉。

translations.literal: You may kill me to surrender to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: You may kill me to surrender to Jin.

sentences.zh: 」父老皆泣，願以死守。

translations.literal: ” The elders all wept and vowed to die defending him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The elders all wept and vowed to die defending him.

sentences.zh: 是時，行周適從行珪在武州，即夜縋行周馳入晉見莊宗，莊宗因遣明宗救武州。

translations.literal: At that time Xingzhou happened to be with Xinggui at Wuzhou; that night he let Xingzhou down the wall and galloped to Jin to see Zhuangzong; Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to rescue Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xingzhou happened to be with Xinggui at Wuzhou. That night he let Xingzhou down the wall and galloped to Jin to see Zhuangzong; Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to rescue Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 比至，行欽已解去，行珪乃降晉。

translations.literal: When they arrived Xingqin had already withdrawn; Xinggui then surrendered to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived Xingqin had already withdrawn; Xinggui then surrendered to Jin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗時，歷朔忻嵐三州刺史、大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: Under Zhuangzong he held in succession Shuozhou, Xinzhou, and Lanzhou prefectures and Datong army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong he held in succession Shuozhou, Xinzhou, and Lanzhou and was Datong army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，徙鎮威勝、安遠。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was moved to Wusheng and Anyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he was moved to Wusheng and Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 行珪性貪鄙，所為多不法，副使範延策，為人剛直，數規諫之，行珪不聽，銜之。

translations.literal: Xinggui was greedy and base; much of what he did was illegal; deputy commissioner Fan Yan’ce was upright and repeatedly admonished him; Xinggui would not listen and bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui was greedy and base; much of what he did was illegal. Deputy commissioner Fan Yan’ce was upright and repeatedly admonished him; Xinggui would not listen and bore resentment.

sentences.zh: 已而戍兵有謀叛者，行珪先覺之，因潛徙庫兵於佗所。

translations.literal: Later garrison troops plotted rebellion; Xinggui detected it first and secretly moved arsenal weapons elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Later garrison troops plotted rebellion. Xinggui detected it first and secretly moved arsenal weapons elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 戍兵叛，趨庫劫兵無所得，乃潰去，行珪追而殺之。

translations.literal: The garrison rebelled, rushed the arsenal to seize weapons and got nothing, then scattered and fled; Xinggui pursued and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison rebelled, rushed the arsenal to seize weapons and got nothing, then scattered and fled. Xinggui pursued and killed them.

sentences.zh: 因誣奏延策同反，並其子皆見殺，天下冤之。

translations.literal: He then falsely memorialized that Yan’ce had joined the rebellion; he and his sons were all killed—the realm considered it a great injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He then falsely memorialized that Yan’ce had joined the rebellion; he and his sons were all killed—the realm considered it a great injustice.

sentences.zh: 行珪卒於鎮，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Xinggui died in his post and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui died in his post and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 當行珪之降晉也，行周隸明宗帳下，初為裨將，趙德鈞識之，謂明宗曰：「此子貌厚而小心，佗日必大貴，宜善待之。

translations.literal: When Xinggui surrendered to Jin, Xingzhou served under Mingzong’s command; at first he was a junior officer. Zhao Dejun recognized him and told Mingzong: “This boy’s face is thick and careful—one day he will be greatly honored; you should treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinggui surrendered to Jin, Xingzhou served under Mingzong’s command; at first he was a junior officer. Zhao Dejun recognized him and told Mingzong: “This boy’s face is thick and careful—one day he will be greatly honored. Treat him well.

sentences.zh: 」梁、晉軍河上，莊宗遣明宗東襲鄆州，行周將前軍，夜遇雨，軍中皆欲止不進，行周曰：「此天贊我也！

translations.literal: ” Liang and Jin armies faced each other on the Yellow River. Zhuangzong sent Mingzong east to strike Yanzhou. Xingzhou led the vanguard. That night it rained; the army all wanted to halt. Xingzhou said: “Heaven is aiding me!
translations.idiomatic: ” Liang and Jin faced each other on the Yellow River. Zhuangzong sent Mingzong east to strike Yanzhou. Xingzhou led the vanguard. That night it rained; the army all wanted to halt. Xingzhou said: “Heaven is aiding me!

sentences.zh: 鄆人恃雨，不備吾來，宜出其不意。

translations.literal: Yan men rely on rain and will not guard against us—strike when they do not expect it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan men rely on rain and will not guard against us—strike when they do not expect it.

sentences.zh: 」即夜馳涉濟，入其城，鄆人方覺，遂取之。

translations.literal: That night he galloped across the ford into the city; the Yan men only then realized it and Yanzhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: That night he galloped across the ford into the city. The Yan men only then realized it—and Yanzhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁，以功領端州刺史，遷絳州。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang; for merit he held Duanzhou prefect, was moved to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang. For merit he held Duanzhou prefect and was moved to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，從平朱守殷，克王都，遷潁州團練使、振武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he followed the pacification of Zhu Shouyin, took Wang Du, was made Yingzhou regimental training commissioner and Zhenwu army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he followed the pacification of Zhu Shouyin, took Wang Du, was made Yingzhou regimental training commissioner and Zhenwu army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷鎮彰武、昭義。

translations.literal: He held in succession Zhangwu and Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He held in succession Zhangwu and Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，為西京留守，徙鎮天雄。

translations.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was western capital regent, was moved to Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was western capital regent, then moved to Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 安從進叛，以行周為襄州行營都部署，討平之，徙鎮歸德。

translations.literal: An Congjin rebelled; Xingzhou was made Xiangzhou field headquarters overall deployer, campaigned and pacified him, was moved to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin rebelled. Xingzhou was made Xiangzhou field headquarters overall deployer, campaigned and pacified him, and was moved to Guide.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，代景延廣為侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Under the Last Emperor he succeeded Jing Yanguang as commander of the personal guard army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 是時，李彥韜、馮玉等用事，乃求歸鎮。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and others held power; he then asked to return to his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and their faction were in charge; he asked to go back to his circuit.

sentences.zh: 契丹滅晉，留蕭翰守汴，翰又棄去，召唐故許王從益入汴。

translations.literal: The Khitan destroyed Jin, left Xiao Han to guard Bian, Han again abandoned it and summoned the former Tang Prince of Xu Congyi into Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan destroyed Jin and left Xiao Han at Bian. Han soon abandoned the city and called in the former Tang Prince of Xu, Congyi.

sentences.zh: 而漢高祖起太原，從益遣人召行周，將以拒漢，行周嘆曰：「衰世難輔，況兒戲乎！

translations.literal: Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan; Congyi sent men to summon Xingzhou to use him against Han. Xingzhou sighed and said: “A declining age is hard to aid—how much more child’s play!
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu rose from Taiyuan. Congyi sent for Xingzhou to hold off the Han army. Xingzhou sighed: “A dying house is hard to prop up—and this is child’s play!

sentences.zh: 」乃不從。

translations.literal: ” He then did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: ” He would not go.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入京師，加行周守中書令，徙鎮天平軍，封臨清王。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu entered the capital, added for Xingzhou the acting Grand Secretariat director post, moved him to Tianping Army, and enfeoffed him Prince of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu took the capital he made Xingzhou acting director of the Grand Secretariat, transferred him to Tianping, and enfeoffed him Prince of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入立，封齊王。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu seized the throne, Xingzhou was made Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書令，追封秦王。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 有子懷德。

translations.literal: He had a son, Huaide.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Huaide.

sentences.zh: 白再榮

translations.literal: Bai Zairong
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zairong

sentences.zh: 白再榮，不知其世家何人也。

translations.literal: Bai Zairong—his family origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zairong—nothing is known of his lineage.

sentences.zh: 少為軍卒。

translations.literal: In youth he was a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 唐、晉之間，為護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: Between Tang and Jin he was commander of the Husheng guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang and Jin he commanded the Husheng guard.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯京師，再榮從契丹北歸，至鎮州，契丹留麻守鎮州而去，晉人從者多留焉。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital, Zairong followed the Khitan north; reaching Zhen prefecture, the Khitan left Ma to hold Zhen and departed, and many Jin followers stayed there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital, Zairong marched north with them. At Zhen prefecture the Khitan left Ma in charge and withdrew; many who had served Jin stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 居未幾，李筠、何福進等謀逐麻，使人召再榮，再榮遲疑不欲往，軍士迫之，乃往，共攻之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Jun, He Fujin, and others plotted to drive Ma out and sent men to summon Zairong. Zairong hesitated and did not wish to go; the soldiers pressed him, and he went and joined in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Jun, He Fujin, and others plotted to expel Ma and sent for Zairong. He hung back until the troops forced him; then he went and joined the assault.

sentences.zh: 麻走，諸將以再榮名次最高，乃推為留後。

translations.literal: Ma fled; the generals, because Zairong ranked highest, pushed him as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Ma fled. The generals, Zairong being senior in rank, made him acting governor.

sentences.zh: 再榮出於行伍，貪而無謀。

translations.literal: Zairong came from the ranks—greedy and without plan.
translations.idiomatic: A ranker risen high—greedy and witless.

sentences.zh: 是時，李崧、和凝等皆隨契丹留鎮州，再榮以兵環其居，迫而求物，又欲害崧取其貲。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yun, He Ning, and others had all stayed at Zhen with the Khitan; Zairong ringed their houses with troops and pressed them for goods, and even wished to kill Yun and take his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun, He Ning, and other court men were still at Zhen with the Khitan. Zairong surrounded their houses with troops and extorted goods; he even meant to kill Yun for his property.

sentences.zh: 李穀謂曰：「公等親被契丹之苦，憂死不暇，然逐麻者，乃眾人所為，非獨公力也。

translations.literal: Li Gu said to him: “You gentlemen yourselves suffered the Khitan’s torment and could not think of death; yet driving out Ma was the crowd’s doing—not yours alone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu told him: “You yourselves barely escaped the Khitan—you had no leisure to fear death. Expelling Ma was the work of the multitude, not yours alone.

sentences.zh: 今才得生路，而遽殺宰相，此契丹尚或不為，然它日至京師，天子問宰相何在，何以對之？

translations.literal: You have just won a way to live and at once would kill a chancellor—even the Khitan might not do that; yet when you reach the capital and the Son of Heaven asks where the chancellor is, how will you answer?
translations.idiomatic: You have barely found a road back to life and would straightway kill a chancellor—even the Khitan might balk at that. When you reach the capital and the emperor asks where the chancellor is, what will you say?

sentences.zh: 」再榮默然，乃止。

translations.literal: ” Zairong was silent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zairong said nothing and desisted.

sentences.zh: 而悉拘嘗事麻者取其財，鎮人謂之「白麻」。

translations.literal: But he seized all who had once served Ma and took their goods; the people of the prefecture called him “White Ma.”
translations.idiomatic: He still seized everyone who had served Ma and stripped their wealth; locals nicknamed him “White Ma.”

sentences.zh: 漢高祖即位，拜再榮為留後，遷義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne, Zairong was confirmed acting governor and later made military commissioner of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu confirmed him as acting governor, then made him military commissioner of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 罷還京師。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周太祖以兵入京師，軍士攻再榮於第，悉取其財。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu marched into the capital with troops, soldiers attacked Zairong at his mansion and stripped all his goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital with an army, soldiers stormed Zairong’s house and looted it bare.

sentences.zh: 已而前啟曰：「士卒嘗事公隸麾下，一旦無禮如此，亦復何面見公乎！

translations.literal: Then they came forward and said: “We once served under you—yet to be treated without courtesy like this, how can we again face you?
translations.idiomatic: They then stepped forward: “We once served in your command—yet you are shown such disrespect. How can we bear to look you in the face?

sentences.zh: 」乃斬之，攜其首而去，家人以帛贖而葬之。

translations.literal: ” They beheaded him and carried off his head; his family ransomed the body with silk and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: ” They cut off his head and left. His kin bought back the corpse with silk and buried him.

sentences.zh: 安叔千

translations.literal: An Shuqian
translations.idiomatic: An Shuqian

sentences.zh: 安叔千，字胤宗，沙陀三部落人也。

translations.literal: An Shuqian, style Yinzong, was a man of the three Shatuo tribes.
translations.idiomatic: An Shuqian, styled Yinzong, came from the three Shatuo tribes.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，事唐莊宗，以為奉安指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at riding and archery; he served Tang Zhuangzong and was made commander of the Feng’an guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at riding and archery. He served Zhuangzong and became commander of the Feng’an guard.

sentences.zh: 明宗時與討王都，拜秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he joined in attacking Wang Du and was made prefect of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he helped crush Wang Du and was made Qin prefect.

sentences.zh: 從擊契丹，為先鋒都指揮使，以功拜昭武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He followed in striking the Khitan and was vanguard commander; for merit he was made military commissioner of Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the Khitan as vanguard commander and, for merit, became military commissioner of Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 歷靜難、橫海、安國、建雄四鎮。

translations.literal: He held in succession the four circuits Jingnan, Henghai, Anguo, and Jianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He held Jingnan, Henghai, Anguo, and Jianxiong in turn.

sentences.zh: 叔千狀貌堂堂，而不通文字，所為鄙陋，人謂之「沒字碑」。

translations.literal: Shuqian had a imposing presence but did not know writing; his conduct was crude, and men called him the “wordless stele.”
translations.idiomatic: Shuqian looked the part of a commander but could not read; his ways were crude, and people called him the “blank stele.”

sentences.zh: 晉出帝時，為左金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Under the Last Emperor of Jin he was senior general of the Left Golden Crow guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Last Emperor he was senior general of the Left Golden Crow guard.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯京師，晉百官迎見耶律德光於赤岡，叔千出班夷言，德光勞曰：「是安沒字否？

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital, Jin’s hundred officials went out to meet Yelü Deguang at Red Mound; Shuqian stepped forward in barbarian speech. Deguang comforted him: “Are you An the Wordless?
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital, Jin officials went out to meet Yelü Deguang at Red Mound. Shuqian spoke to him in Khitan. Deguang said kindly: “So you are An the Wordless?

sentences.zh: 汝在邢州，已通誠款，吾今至此，當與汝一吃飯處。

translations.literal: You at Xing prefecture already opened good faith to me; now that I have come here, I shall give you a place to eat.
translations.idiomatic: At Xing prefecture you already showed good faith. Now that I am here, I will find you a seat at table.

sentences.zh: 」叔千再拜。

translations.literal: ” Shuqian bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shuqian bowed low again.

sentences.zh: 乃以為鎮國軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was then made military commissioner of Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入立，罷歸京師，自以常私附契丹，頗懷愧懼。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne, Shuqian was dismissed and returned to the capital; he himself had often secretly sided with the Khitan and was quite ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu recalled him to the capital. He had often courted the Khitan in secret and was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 以太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 周太祖兵入京師，軍士大掠，叔千家貲已盡，而軍士意其有所藏者，箠掠不已。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu’s troops entered the capital, soldiers plundered widely; Shuqian’s household goods were already gone, yet the troops thought he still had hidden stores and beat him without end.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu’s army entered the capital, troops looted the city. Shuqian’s house was already empty, but soldiers believed he still had hoards and flogged him without cease.

sentences.zh: 傷重，歸於洛陽，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Grievously wounded, he returned to Luoyang and died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Badly hurt, he went home to Luoyang and died at seventy-two.
